authors: Vaswani, A.; Shazeer, N.; Parmar, N.; Uszkoreit, J.; Jones, L.; Gomez, A. N.; Kaiser, L.; Polosukhin, I.
architecture: Transformer: encoder-decoder built only from multi-head self-attention (no recurrence/convolution)
key_results: Reported higher BLEU at lower training cost than prior recurrent/convolutional models (abstract-level)
limitations: Not an RL or control paper; self-attention cost quadratic in sequence length

authors: Zaheer, M.; Kottur, S.; Ravanbakhsh, S.; Poczos, B.; Salakhutdinov, R.; Smola, A.
architecture: Deep Sets: sum-decomposition rho(sum phi(x)) characterised as the form of permutation-invariant functions; permutation-equivariant layers
environment_or_data: Population statistics, point clouds, set expansion, image tagging
key_results: Theorem characterising permutation-invariant set functions; architecture applies to sets of any cardinality (abstract-level)
limitations: Not RL; sum pooling has limited interaction modelling between elements

authors: Lee, J.; Lee, Y.; Kim, J.; Kosiorek, A. R.; Choi, S.; Teh, Y. W.
architecture: Set Transformer: attention-based permutation-invariant encoder/decoder; inducing-point attention reduces cost from quadratic to linear in set size
environment_or_data: Multiple-instance learning, 3D shape recognition, few-shot classification
key_results: Attention captures interactions among set elements; inducing points give linear-time attention (abstract-level)

authors: Kool, W.; van Hoof, H.; Welling, M.
problem: Routing combinatorial optimisation (TSP, VRP variants, OP, PCTSP)
architecture: Attention-based encoder-decoder over node tokens (variable number of nodes)
environment_or_data: Synthetic routing instances up to 100 nodes
baselines: Pointer networks, learned heuristics, specialised solvers
key_results: Near-optimal TSP up to 100 nodes; one hyper-parameter set works across several routing problems (abstract-level); abstract does not claim size generalisation
limitations: Abstract makes no zero-shot size-transfer claim

authors: Hu, S.; Zhu, F.; Chang, X.; Liang, X.
problem: Multi-agent RL across tasks with different numbers of agents/entities
architecture: UPDeT: transformer over observation entities; policy decoupling maps attention outputs to entity-related actions
environment_or_data: StarCraft multi-agent tasks of different sizes (e.g. 3v3, 5v6 per abstract)
key_results: One architecture handles different observation/action configurations and transfers across tasks (abstract-level)

authors: Yang, Y.; Luo, R.; Li, M.; Zhou, M.; Zhang, W.; Wang, J.
architecture: Each agent conditions on its own state and the mean action of the population/neighbours
environment_or_data: Resource allocation, Ising model, battle game
key_results: Population interaction approximated by agent vs. average effect; convergence analysed (abstract-level)

authors: Joshi, C. K.; Cappart, Q.; Rousseau, L.-M.; Laurent, T.
problem: Zero-shot generalisation of neural TSP solvers to larger instances
method: Controlled study of NCO pipelines (architectures, SL vs RL, decoding)
architecture: GNN / attention encoders with autoregressive or non-autoregressive decoders
environment_or_data: Synthetic TSP instances, train small / test larger
baselines: Classical solvers and recent learned solvers
key_results: Learned TSP policies trained on small graphs fail to extrapolate to larger instances unless inductive biases/pipeline are rethought (abstract-level)

authors: Luo, F.; Lin, X.; Liu, F.; Wang, Z.; Zhang, Q.
problem: Large-scale generalisation of constructive neural CO
architecture: LEHD: light encoder, heavy attention decoder re-attending to remaining nodes of varying size
environment_or_data: TSP, CVRP up to 1000 nodes; TSPLib, CVRPLib
key_results: Trained on small instances, near-optimal on TSP/CVRP up to 1000 nodes (abstract-level)
limitations: Not RL control; no hard physical constraints

authors: Sadeghianpourhamami, N.; Deleu, J.; Develder, C.
problem: Joint coordination of EV charging at a set of charging stations (load flattening)
architecture: FC network (128-64) on aggregate binned state: grid of EV counts by time-to-departure x remaining charging time, normalised by N_max
environment_or_data: ElaadNL real charging sessions (Netherlands); 2 h slots, 24 h horizon
baselines: Business-as-usual; oracle QP optimum with perfect information
key_results: 10/50 stations: cost reduction vs BAU 39%/30.4% vs optimum 52%; gap to optimum 13%/15.6%; policy trained with N_max=10 evaluated on arrivals scaled up to 10x with largest cost increase at 2x (Sec. VI-C, Fig. 6)
limitations: Load flattening only; one charging rate per group; infeasibility via penalty; action space exponential in S_max; one dataset

authors: Tuchnitz, F.; Ebell, N.; Schlund, J.; Pruckner, M.
problem: Smart charging coordination of an EV fleet considering grid baseload
method: Deep RL (value-based with prioritised experience variants)
architecture: Central agent with neural network function approximator producing schedules for a fleet of any size (abstract)
baselines: Uncontrolled charging; optimisation-based strategy with perfect information; other strategies
key_results: Load variance reduced by 65% vs uncontrolled; all EVs reported sufficiently charged at departure; close to optimisation benchmark (abstract-level)
limitations: Abstract does not report training vs test fleet sizes; constraint satisfaction empirical

authors: Ye, Z.; Gao, Y.; Yu, N.
problem: Profit-maximising operation of an EV charging station with V2G
method: CADE: centralised allocation + decentralised execution; DQN
architecture: One DQN (256-128-64) shared by all homogeneous chargers with a shared replay memory; per-charger state incl. station-level summary features
constraint_handling: penalty+other:feasible discrete action set per charger
environment_or_data: Synthetic Poisson arrivals for office/residential/highway/retail sites
baselines: MPC (1 h/2 h), MPC-ideal, greedy urgency heuristic (with/without V2G)
key_results: Beats all baselines except MPC-ideal; sizes 10-100 chargers evaluated with per-step compute 0.7-1.7 ms vs MPC 3-935 s; text does not clearly state whether one trained model was reused across sizes
limitations: Departure energy via shortfall penalty; station peak only via demand charge; synthetic data; homogeneous chargers

authors: Zhang, Y.; Chen, X.; Zhang, Y.
problem: Large-scale V2G charging/discharging coordination by an EV aggregator with renewables
architecture: Aggregator-level MLP: state = 24 h load history, aggregate SOC, load variance; scalar aggregate power action; rule-based dispatch to EVs
key_results: Load variance -97.37% vs uncontrolled (509 EVs); policy reported transferable from 509 EVs to 5,090-50,900 EVs with loads scaled 100x (Sec. V-A); retraining vs direct transfer compared only at 509 EVs
limitations: Not peer-reviewed; several internal numeric inconsistencies; departure times not in state; aggregate SOC/tie-line limits not explicitly enforced

authors: Yan, L.; Chen, X.; Chen, Y.; Wen, J.
problem: Cooperative residential EV charging avoiding transformer overload
method: Decentralised MARL (Markov game) with SAC independent learners
architecture: Per-EV agent: collective-policy model approximating other agents' aggregate consumption + independent SAC learner on local observation
environment_or_data: Real-world-data-based numerical studies (price, residential load, driver behaviour)
key_results: Fully decentralised and claimed scalable to many agents (abstract-level); abstract does not state whether trained weights were tested at another EV count
limitations: Abstract only; constraint treatment not described in abstract

authors: Wang, M.; Feng, M.; Zhou, W.; Li, H.
problem: Active voltage control in distribution networks with PV inverters
architecture: Transformer policy with bus tokens, adjacency-masked attention, agent-centric readout; parameters shared across agents with agent ID; transformer critic over agents
key_results: Controllable rate e.g. 141-bus spring 75.8%->97.8% (MADDPG), 322-bus spring 59.4%->90.6% (MATD3) (Table 1); each network trained separately, no cross-size transfer
limitations: Per-network training; soft barrier penalties; CR below 100%

authors: Jin, B.; Sun, S.; Zhang, Y.; Zheng, S.; Yu, H.
problem: Zero-shot active voltage control across distribution feeders under imperfect telemetry
method: TD3-style graph actor-critic (GRAS-AVC) with imitation and risk terms
architecture: Permutation-equivariant shared actor: 3 edge-conditioned message-passing layers, shared per-inverter head, droop prior + residual; variable-size twin graph critics (mean/max pooling)
environment_or_data: 7 source feeders (15-141 buses) for training; zero-shot 322-bus target (38 DERs)
baselines: Droop, matched Graph-TD3 (with/without selector), feeder-specific MATD3
key_results: Same weights 15-141 buses -> 322 buses (6->38 DERs); violating bus-time 7.455% (droop) -> 2.723% with runtime AC power-flow screening
limitations: One-step screening not a multi-step certificate; one target feeder; 5 seeds; requires physical model at deployment

authors: Yan, H.; Ding, S.; Zhang, J.; Yao, X.; Liu, Y.; Wang, H.; Luo, C.; Shi, Y.
problem: Spatio-temporal V2G scheduling inside optimal power flow with hard grid and EV demand constraints
method: HPC-RL: GRG-SAC upper level + dynamic-boundary lower level
architecture: Network type not specified; upper policy outputs basic OPF variables, non-basic via Newton solve; lower level computes per-EV feasible power bounds
constraint_handling: projection+other:generalised reduced gradient and dynamic per-EV bounds
environment_or_data: IEEE 14, 30, modified 141-bus; PyTorch simulator; fixed EV profiles
key_results: Objective gap to MPC ~7-13%; runtime 0.87-4.97 s vs MPC 309-5173 s; 100% demand satisfaction; small nonzero equality violations (Table 3); no cross-size transfer test
limitations: Prop. 1 only first-order tangent-space feasibility; demand guarantee claimed without proof; infeasible arrivals not addressed; speed-up figures inconsistent

problem: Decentralised mid-shift charging decisions in electric delivery fleets with station congestion
method: NEAT and PPO with a shared per-vehicle policy
architecture: Per-candidate scorer applied to each of up to 5 nearby stations (invariant to candidate count) or padded joint MLP; hand-built margin/occupancy signals
environment_or_data: Discrete-event simulator on OpenStreetMap networks of 20 cities
baselines: Oracle (simulated annealing with future knowledge), greedy, null, tuned threshold rule
key_results: Trained on 4 cities, zero-shot on 16 unseen cities (3-10 stations, ~21-138 vehicles); fleet density swept 5-50 EVs/station without retraining; queue wait ~45 min (greedy) -> ~2 min
limitations: Not peer-reviewed; SoC floor only via reward; routing surrogate error; simulation only

authors: Caballe, J.; Segovia, P.; Ocampo-Martinez, C.; Quijano, N.
problem: Large-scale EV charging coordination with nodal capacity limits and battery degradation
method: Comparison of mean-field games / mean-field-type games vs classical and deep RL
architecture: Mean-field policies depending on population statistics; RL agents (details not in abstract)
environment_or_data: 3-node one-night grid; 7-day heterogeneous 1,000-EV testbed on real distribution data
key_results: Mean-field-type games minimise unmet energy and queueing; DRL highest average final SOC (~81%) under volatile tariffs (abstract-level); mean-field policies epsilon-Nash as fleet grows

authors: Hassouna, M.; Holzhuter, C.; Lytaev, P.; Thomas, J.; Sick, B.; Scholz, C.
problem: Survey of graph RL for transmission and distribution grid control
architecture: GNN-based RL (graph structures, GNN types, RL algorithms)
key_results: Graph RL shows adaptability to unpredictable events/noisy data but remains mostly proof-of-concept (abstract-level)
